V_zero_T.field: radial field W >= 0 of Phi = W e^{i theta}/sqrt2, kinetic term (dW)^2/2 as in the action, potential U(W) = z^2 q(z), z = (W/W0)^2 - 1, q from the forward chain (closure/nvg_forward_band.scalar_jet), false vacuum W0 = 859 MeV (U = 0)
V_zero_T.bounce: Euclidean O(4) bounce W'' + (3/r) W' = dU/dW, W'(0) = 0, W(inf) = W0; overshoot/undershoot shooting on ln(W(0) - W_t) with the linearised start W - W_t ~ 2 I1(m_t r)/(m_t r) near the true-vacuum side (thin-wall safe); B = 2 pi^2 int r^3 [W'^2/2 + U - U(W0)] dr, cross-checked by the virial form B = (pi^2/2) int r^3 W'^2 dr (Derrick, d = 4) and by the Coleman-Glaser-Martin upper bound B <= T^2/(-4 V) for trial profiles (T = 2 pi^2 int r^3 W'^2/2, V = 2 pi^2 int r^3 (U - U(W0)))
V_zero_T.gauge_field: S_E = int [F^2/4 + (dW)^2/2 + W^2 (d theta - q_phi A)^2/2 + U(W)] + baryon terms; for n = 0 the extra terms are >= 0 and vanish for theta = const, A = 0, which solves the Maxwell/Proca and theta equations because the current W^2 (d theta - q_phi A) then vanishes. Hence the radial bounce with A = 0 is a solution of the full tree-level system and no gauge or Goldstone configuration lowers its action: B_gauged = B_radial at tree level (the vector mass q_phi W only changes the one-loop prefactor).

cases.a_bounded_with_deeper_state: U bounded below on W >= 0 and U < U(W0) somewhere: bounce computed in each direction (W < W0 and W > W0) that has U < U(W0); B = the smaller action
cases.b_unbounded_below: leading coefficient of q < 0, U ~ a_d (W/W0)^(2d) -> -inf: the tunnelling exponent is the mountain-pass value; for growth faster than W^4 (NVG: d >= 4, U ~ y^8 or y^10) the CGM ratio T^2/(-4V) of profiles W0 (1 + A g(r/R)) falls as A^(4-2d) -> 0 for A -> inf, so B = 0 (no exponential protection; decay controlled by field values far outside the model). For exactly quartic growth (NL3, g3 < 0) B_inf = 8 pi^2 / (3 |g3|) (Fubini) or lower if a finite bounce exists; computed numerically.
cases.c_absolutely_stable: U >= U(W0) for all W >= 0: B = +inf (passes)

V_zero_T.rate: Gamma = A exp(-B) per volume, A bracketed by m_sigma,vac^4 (m_sigma,vac = sqrt(U_yy(1))/W0) and W0^4; requirement Gamma t_U^4 < 1, t_U = 13.8 Gyr (1 Gyr = 3.15576e16 s, hbar = 6.582119569e-22 MeV s) -> B > B_thr(A) = ln(A t_U^4). PASS iff B > B_thr(W0^4) (the upper end of the bracket, conservative); 'bracket-dependent' reported if B_thr(m^4) < B <= B_thr(W0^4). Sensitivity (not criterion): Callan-Coleman translational factor (B/2pi)^2 in A.

V_thermal.bounce: O(3) bounce W'' + (2/r) W' = dU_T/dW, B3 = 4 pi int r^2 [W'^2/2 + U_T - U_T(false)] dr (virial cross-check B3 = (4 pi/3) int r^2 W'^2 dr)
V_thermal.potential: primary U_T(W) = U(W) + f_N(T, M_N W/W0) - f_N(T, M_N): one-loop thermal free energy of the nucleon doublet at zero chemical potential (g = 8: p, n, spin, particle + antiparticle), f_N = -(g T/(2 pi^2)) int k^2 ln(1 + exp(-E/T)) dk; variant: tree-level U only
V_thermal.rate_and_requirement: Gamma_T = T^4 (B3/(2 pi T))^(3/2) exp(-B3/T); nucleation probability P = Gamma_T V_core dt < 1 with V_core = (4 pi/3) (10 km)^3 and dt = 1e10 yr (one stellar core held at T for 1e10 yr: conservative). Also reported: the rate with prefactor W0^4 and the total over 1e20 hot cores x 10 s; the zero-T O(4) channel at the same T (Gamma_4 V_core dt) is reported alongside.
V_thermal.pass: P < 1 at every declared T (with the T^4 prefactor), using min over the O(3) thermal and O(4) channels

G_dense_matter.primary: the existing ground-state condition of prereg.json nvg_class.ground_state_valid ((a) beta table x_match <= x <= x_c(M_max), (b) SNM at x = 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, (c) SNM and PNM at 0.10 fm^-3: tracked state is the global minimum over y), with the y grid extended from [0.02, 1.4] to [0.02, max(1.4, 1.25 y_t)] whenever the vacuum's deeper state y_t lies beyond 1.4 (the declared definition is 'global minimum over y'; the old grid end was chosen for U >= 0 models)
G_dense_matter.variant_G_meta_declared_not_primary: nodes where the tracked state is not the global minimum are accepted if the in-medium O(4) bounce of the grand potential Omega(y; mu) = U(y) + min_n [eps_N(n, y) - mu n] (fixed baryon chemical potential mu of the node, fixed composition delta of the node, vector field in local density approximation, nucleon gradient terms neglected) has B_med > ln(A V_core t) with A = W0^4, V_core = (4 pi/3) (10 km)^3, t = 13.8 Gyr. derivation.bounce: Euclidean O(4) bounce of the radial field W (kinetic (dW)^2/2): W'' + 3W'/r = dU/dW, W'(0) = 0, W(inf) = W0. With y = W/W0, rho = r sqrt(Lambda)/W0, u = U/Lambda (Lambda = a2): B = (W0^4/Lambda) 2 pi^2 int rho^3 [y'^2/2 + u] d rho = (W0^4/Lambda) pi^2 int rho^3 y'^2 d rho (Derrick virial, d = 4).
derivation.gauge_field: S_E = int [F^2/4 + (dW)^2/2 + W^2 (d theta - q_phi A)^2/2 + U(W)]; for n = 0 the extra terms are non-negative and vanish at theta = const, A = 0, which solves the Proca and theta equations because the current W^2 (d theta - q_phi A) then vanishes. The radial bounce is therefore a solution of the full tree-level system and no gauge/Goldstone configuration lowers its action: B_gauged = B_radial (the vector mass q_phi W enters only the one-loop prefactor). The baryon term C_v n^2/(2 y^2) vanishes at n = 0.
derivation.unbounded_case: If the leading coefficient of q is negative, U ~ a_d y^(2d) -> -inf with 2d = 8 (quartic) or 10 (quintic). For profiles y = 1 + A g(r/R) the Coleman-Glaser-Martin ratio T^2/(-4V) is r-scale invariant and falls as A^(4-2d) -> 0, so the mountain-pass exponent is B = 0 (no protection). For exactly quartic growth (NL3) the limit is the Fubini value 8 pi^2/(3|g3|).

thresholds.note: m_sigma,vac = sqrt(U_yy(1))/W0 = 70-110 MeV for the NVG jets, so the A bracket moves B_thr by <= 10

derivation.thermal: O(3) bounce in U_T = U + f_N(T, M y) - f_N(T, M) (nucleon doublet, g = 8, mu = 0); Gamma_T = T^4 (B3/(2 pi T))^(3/2) exp(-B3/T); P = Gamma_T V_core dt, V_core = (4 pi/3)(10 km)^3, dt = 1e10 yr. For the NVG deeper states at y > 1 the nucleon thermal term is negligible (heavier nucleons inside the bubble): B3 with and without it agree within 6.4 percent for all 33 tested members and T <= 50 MeV.

verdict_text: Replacing absolute stability by metastability (Gamma t_U^4 < 1, B > 384.6) adds zero parameters but opens almost nothing useful. The quartic below y* = 0.8657 is unbounded below as y^8 (B = 0), so the rule falls back to the quintic. Under the new rule the opened m*/M are 0.61-0.62 at the low end and 0.76-0.87 at the high end. The thermal check removes 0.62 and every member with B <= 900. The spin-orbit band m*/M = 0.63-0.75 stays closed: the largest B there is 288 at 0.63, falling to 43 at 0.70. m*/M = 0.55-0.60 was already open as an absolutely stable quintic, and those members fail everywhere else (R_1.4 = 15.7-16.7 km, chi2 >= 293, O = 1.3-1.5 MeV because y(n) is discontinuous below n0). Every metastable member (108/108) fails the existing ground-state condition (G): its deeper vacuum (y = 0 or y = 1.2-1.85) is also, dressed by matter, the ground state of nuclear matter, in 87 cases inside the stellar core. So the G-valid reopened class is the stable class: lnZ = -13.49, ppc p = 0.069, LOO J0740 mass z = +2.54, J0614 radius z = -2.18. It fails by leave-one-out, as before. No member of any subset passes the 16O spin-orbit window (max 2.74 MeV). Dropping (G) entirely, which bounds what the declared G_meta variant could achieve, raises lnZ to -11.52 but still fails (LOO J0614 z = -2.52, O 0 passes), so the conditional verdict is also negative. Consistency check: NL3's own sigma potential fails the same criterion far worse (an actual bounce with B = 0.877 towards M* ~ 31 M). NL3 is usable only because its U stays above the vacuum on -1.06 < M*/M < 2.03, a domain that contains all of its matter. The NVG metastable members are not rescued by that domain logic, because their deeper states lie inside the range their own matter explores (G fails).
practical_value: Validated O(4)/O(3) bounce solver for one real field with thin-wall-safe linearised start (bounce.py): Coleman thin wall within 0.08 percent after extrapolation to eps -> 0, cubic 204.4 vs 204.8-205, Adams 1993 fit within 0.075 percent, Fubini exact within 4e-5
Thresholds: B > 384.6 (A = W0^4) or 375 (A = (70-80 MeV)^4) for Gamma t_U^4 < 1; B3/T > 215-222 for one 10-km core at 10-50 MeV for 1e10 yr; in-medium B > 233
NVG vacuum map B(y*, Q0, n0, E/A, K) (structure_map.jsonl): quartic unbounded for y* < 0.8657; quintic metastable windows; the closed band 0.63-0.75
NL3 literal vacuum decays (B = 0.88): RMF sigma potentials with g3 < 0 should be quoted with their field domain (U > U_vac for -1.06 < M*/M < 2.03), not as metastable vacua
A metastable vacuum in an NVG jet always propagates into the matter ground state (G): metastability does not separate the vacuum question from the Lee-Wick question in this action
caveats: tree level: the nucleon Dirac-sea (Coleman-Weinberg) term is absent (no-sea), as in RMF; it would add -y^4 ln y pieces at large W
B = 0 for unbounded members is a statement about field values W >> W0, outside any trusted domain
